body: LLMs are increasingly used as AI tutors, yet existing benchmarks overlook the challenging behaviors common among students with learning and behavioral difficulties. We introduce TutorCaseBench, a benchmark that grounds AI-tutor evaluation in qualitative case studies from pedagogy, educational psychology, and special education. Our pipeline converts documented student categories into case-specific scenarios, tutor-student dialogues, and rubrics grounded in source evidence. The benchmark contains 923 dialogues across five challenge types, evaluated through open-ended response generation (1,560 items) and multiple-choice selection (2,537 items). Across 11 state-of-the-art LLMs, even the strongest model satisfies a rubric criterion in only 55.8% of open-ended cases, while models are better at selecting appropriate strategies than generating situated responses. These results reveal a gap between intervention recognition and context-specific adaptation, especially for open-weight models. All data are publicly available at https://github.com/kixlab/TutorCaseBench.
summaryZh: TutorCaseBench：评估 LLM 导师支持具有挑战性行为的学生的案例基准。LLM 越来越多地被用作 AI 导师，但现有基准忽视了学习和行为困难学生中常见的挑战性行为。我们推出了 TutorCaseBench，这是一个基准，它将人工智能导师评估建立在教育学、教育心理学和特殊教育的定性案例研究中。
